en: Therīgāthā 5.8 Pañcakanipāta Soṇātherīgāthā The Verses of the Elder Nun Soṇā, from the Fifth Chapter: The Group of Five I have crossed over the flood; I am free from craving. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell in peace. I have reached the further shore of birth and death; I am a nun who has attained liberation. I was born into a family of great wealth, Possessing much gold and many treasures. But seeing the suffering inherent in worldly existence, I went forth into homelessness out of faith. My father, my mother, and my husband, As well as my children and grandchildren— To all of them I said farewell, And I departed from home for the sake of the Dhamma. When I had gone forth, I practiced with diligence; I cultivated the path that leads to peace. By means of this noble practice, I have realized the state of an arahant. I have cut off the stream of rebirth; I have destroyed the fetters of existence. I am cooled and at peace; There is no more renewed becoming for me. I am one who has done what was to be done; I have laid down the heavy burden. Through the destruction of craving, I am liberated; I have attained the final Nibbāna. I am a nun who has attained liberation; I am one who has reached the goal. I pay homage to the Teacher, Who is the Buddha, the Fully Awakened One. I pay homage to the Dhamma, Which is well-expounded and leads to peace. I pay homage to the Saṅgha, The community of the noble ones, practicing rightly. I have seen the Truth; I have known the Truth; I have understood the Truth and have penetrated it. “Having given birth to ten sons in this collection of forms,
I have now become weak and aged.”
I approached a bhikkhunī;
she taught me the Dhamma:
the aggregates, the sense bases, and the elements.
Having heard her Dhamma,
I cut my hair and went forth.
While I was still a trainee (sikkhamānā),...
The divine eye has been purified;
I know my former abodes,
where I dwelt in the past.
I cultivated the signless state,
one-pointed and well-composed;
I attained the immediate liberation.
They have attained extinction through non-clinging.
The five aggregates, fully understood,
remain with their roots cut off.
“Praise be to old age and birth;
now there is no further becoming.
Thus spoke the elder nun Soṇā.
